how: cargo xtask compare: the conformance tests of emulator/rs/scenarios (cargo spec, cargo ble-spec) run in the Outglow emulator on the original firmware images and on Outglow images built from this repository

suites.covers: Zigbee: Zigbee PRO R22, Zigbee Cluster Library revision 8, Base Device Behavior 3.0.1, Lighting & Occupancy 1.0, Green Power Basic 1.1.2
Bluetooth LE: Bluetooth Core Specification 5.4 and the Core Specification Supplement

tests.requirement: A data frame received with the acknowledgement request bit set is answered with an APS acknowledgement: same cluster, profile and APS counter, endpoints swapped, no acknowledgement request, ack format bit clear.
A frame received with the acknowledgement request bit clear is not acknowledged (it is still delivered).
A frame received a second time (same source and APS counter, 0.5 s later) is delivered to the application only once, and is acknowledged again.

All retransmissions the text defines are recognised as duplicates: a sender whose acknowledgements are lost repeats the frame apscMaxFrameRetries = 3 times, every apscAckWaitDuration = 1.6 s (copies 1.6, 3.2 and 4.8 s after the original).
The last retransmission alone (4.8 s after the original, the two before it lost on the way) is still recognised as a duplicate.

tests.requirement: The APS counter is incremented by one for each new transmission.
A group-addressed frame (delivery mode 0b11) is delivered to an endpoint that is a member of the group, and not delivered when no endpoint is a member.
A unicast frame with destination endpoint 0xff is presented to all endpoints 1-254 of the device; a frame for an endpoint the device does not have reaches no application.
A transmission due to a binding with a unicast destination goes to the network address of that device with delivery mode 0b00 and the destination endpoint of the binding.
A transmission due to a binding with a group destination has delivery mode 0b11, the group address in the APS header, no destination endpoint, no acknowledgement request, and is broadcast to 0xfffd.
A data frame that carries the extended header sub-frame with fragmentation = 0b00 (not fragmented, no block number) is an ordinary frame and is delivered like one.

tests.requirement: A router that has joined activates its own permit joining flag for at least bdbcMinCommissioningTime (180 s): its beacon offers association right after the join and still does 100 s later.

After receiving the network key the node broadcasts Device_annce to 0xFFFD with its network address, IEEE address and the capability information it associated with (router: FFD, receiver on when idle, allocate address = 1).

On a centralized network whose Trust Center reports revision 21 or later, the joined node asks for the Trust Center's node descriptor, requests a new link key (Request Key, key type 4, APS-encrypted with the initial link key) and verifies the key it gets (Verify Key with the hash of the new key).

After joining (and the link key exchange) the node broadcasts Mgmt_Permit_Joining_req with PermitDuration of at least 180 s and TC_Significance 1; the broadcast addressing of this request is 'all routers and coordinator' (0xFFFC).

dimm.stock_note: PermitDuration 180 s and TC_Significance 1 are right, but the request is broadcast to 0xffff; R22 2.4.3.3.7.1 names 'all routers and coordinator' (0xFFFC)

tw.stock_note: PermitDuration 180 s and TC_Significance 1 are right, but the request is broadcast to 0xffff; R22 2.4.3.3.7.1 names 'all routers and coordinator' (0xFFFC)

tests.requirement: The permit joining flag activated after the join stays on for bdbcMinCommissioningTime: 100 s after the join the beacon still offers association.
A node that is not on a network joins only networks whose beacon has permit joining set: it does not try to associate with a closed network, and joins once the network opens.

On a unicast Image Notify an OTA Upgrade client always sends a Query Next Image Request to the upgrade server, carrying its manufacturer code, its image type and the file version of the image it runs (here: those of the OTA file built with the image), no wild card.

tests.requirement: A router that receives a unicast NWK Leave with request = 1 and rejoin = 0 announces its own leave (MAC broadcast, NWK destination 0xFFFD, radius 1, request = 0, rejoin = 0, source IEEE address) and is then no longer on the network.
A router that receives a unicast NWK Leave with request = 1 and rejoin = 1 announces its leave with request = 0 and the rejoin flag copied (1).

A device that left with rejoin = 1 may rejoin: its Rejoin Request goes to the prospective parent with radius 1, its IEEE address in the NWK header and its capability information; after a successful Rejoin Response it operates on the network again under the address the response carries.

tests.ambiguous: no clause obliges a router to notice by itself that the network moved to a key it does not have; INCONCLUSIVE when the bulb never tries
tests.requirement: A device that missed a network key update can get back by a Trust Center rejoin: an unsecured Rejoin Request, then the unsecured Rejoin Response and the active network key under its link key bring it back onto the network.
A NWK Leave with request = 1 that was sent to a broadcast address is dropped.

A unicast Mgmt_Leave_req naming the device itself is answered with Mgmt_Leave_rsp SUCCESS before the device leaves; the device then announces its leave (request = 0, rejoin = 0) and is no longer on the network.
A Mgmt_Leave_req that was sent to a broadcast address is dropped: no response, no leave.
A Mgmt_Leave_req naming a device that is neither the router itself nor one of its children does not make the router leave; the response carries an error status.

tests.ambiguous: address conflict detection is enabled when nwkUniqueAddr is FALSE; R22 Table 3-58 gives TRUE as the default and the Zigbee PRO stack profile (not among the suite's documents) sets FALSE
tests.requirement: A frame addressed to the device's network address whose destination IEEE address is not the device's own reveals a local address conflict: the router broadcasts a Network Status 0x0d to 0xFFFD with its previous address, picks a new address and announces it.

dimm.stock_note: no Network Status 'address conflict' after a frame for the bulb's address with another device's IEEE address in the NWK header, nor after a broadcast from another device under the bulb's network address

tw.stock_note: no Network Status 'address conflict' after a frame for the bulb's address with another device's IEEE address in the NWK header, nor after a broadcast from another device under the bulb's network address

tests.ambiguous: the value of nwkNetworkBroadcastDeliveryTime follows from stack profile parameters (commonly 9 s); the test only requires that the old PAN identifier is still in use 1 s after the command and that the new one is in use within 60 s
tests.requirement: On a Network Update command (PAN identifier update) the device starts a timer of nwkNetworkBroadcastDeliveryTime and changes its PAN identifier only when it expires; the copies of the command it relays still go out under the old PAN identifier.

dimm.stock_note: the bulb relayed the Network Update under PAN 0x2b7c 34 ms after receiving it; it must go out under the old PAN identifier 0x1a62

tw.stock_note: the bulb relayed the Network Update under PAN 0x2b7c 10 ms after receiving it; it must go out under the old PAN identifier 0x1a62

tests.requirement: A Mgmt_NWK_Update_req with ScanDuration 0xFE and a single supported channel makes the device change to that channel.

A router sends a Link Status command at least every nwkLinkStatusPeriod (15 s) as a one-hop broadcast without retries: destination 0xFFFC, radius 1; a status that fits one frame has the first and last frame bits set, and the entries are sorted by ascending address.
The outgoing cost a router reports for a neighbour is the incoming cost that neighbour last reported for it; when the neighbour's Link Status does not list the router, the outgoing cost becomes 0.

A router retransmits a new broadcast whose radius is still above zero after decrementing it: same source and sequence number, MAC broadcast without acknowledgement request, after a random jitter of at most nwkcMaxBroadcastJitter (0x40 ms).

tests.ambiguous: nwkMaxBroadcastRetries is a NIB attribute (R22 default 3; the Zigbee PRO stack profile, not among the suite's documents, is known to set 2), and 'shall retransmit a previously broadcast frame at most nwkMaxBroadcastRetries times' can count the first relay or not; the test accepts 2 to 4 transmissions when no neighbour relays the frame
tests.requirement: While neighbours have not relayed a broadcast, the router keeps retransmitting it, nwkMaxBroadcastRetries times in all.

dimm.stock_note: 1 transmission(s) (gaps [] ms) of a broadcast that the two router neighbours never relayed

tw.stock_note: 1 transmission(s) (gaps [] ms) of a broadcast that the two router neighbours never relayed

tests.requirement: A broadcast received with radius 1 is delivered to the application but not retransmitted; a second copy of a broadcast already in the broadcast transaction table is dropped (neither delivered again nor retransmitted).

dimm.stock_note: a second copy of a broadcast (2500 ms after the first, same source and sequence number, different APS counter) was delivered to the application again (two Toggles executed)

tw.stock_note: a second copy of a broadcast (2500 ms after the first, same source and sequence number, different APS counter) was delivered to the application again (two Toggles executed)

tests.requirement: A router that is not the destination of a Route Request rebroadcasts it with the link cost of the previous hop added to the path cost (same identifier, destination and NWK source), after a jitter, and retries the relay nwkcRREQRetries (2) more times.

A router that is not the originator of a route discovery forwards the Route Reply to the next hop towards the originator, adding the cost of that link to the path cost and keeping identifier, originator and responder.

With an active routing table entry a router relays a unicast frame to the next hop: MAC unicast with 16-bit addresses, NWK sequence number unchanged, radius decremented; a frame whose radius falls to 0 is not relayed.

tests.ambiguous: nwkSymLink is FALSE by default in R22 Table 3-58 and set to TRUE by the Zigbee PRO stack profile, which is not among the documents the suite reads
tests.requirement: With nwkSymLink = TRUE a router that relays a Route Reply also creates the reverse routing table entry, so frames from the responder to the originator are relayed.

A router that is the destination of a Route Request answers with a Route Reply unicast to the device the request came from: originator and identifier from the request, itself as responder, path cost = cost of the link to that next hop (1-7, not 0).

A router that starts a route discovery broadcasts the Route Request with path cost 0 and, while no reply comes, repeats it nwkcInitialRREQRetries (3) times at intervals of nwkcRREQRetryInterval (254 ms).

dimm.stock_note: 5 transmissions of the request (gaps [255, 254, 254, 254] ms); the initial broadcast plus nwkcInitialRREQRetries = 4

tw.stock_note: 5 transmissions of the request (gaps [255, 254, 254, 254] ms); the initial broadcast plus nwkcInitialRREQRetries = 4

tests.requirement: After a many-to-one Route Request (no route cache) a router relays the request and, before its next unicast data frame to that concentrator, unicasts a Route Record with itself as source and relay count 0.
A many-to-one Route Request received from a device that is not in the neighbour table (or whose outgoing cost is 0) is discarded.

A source-routed frame whose relay index is 0 is relayed directly to the NWK destination; with a relay index above 0 and the router's address at that index, the index is decremented and the frame goes to the relay listed before it.

When a relayed frame cannot be delivered to the next relay of its source route, the router sends a Network Status to the source of the frame whose destination address field is the NWK destination of the failed frame.

tests.ambiguous: for a frame without a route and with discover route = 0, 3.6.3.3 first says the frame 'shall be discarded' (naming only the local confirm) and then, in its last paragraph, that a router failing to deliver a relayed frame 'for any reason' shall send a Network Status to its source; the test follows the last paragraph
tests.requirement: When a frame relayed for another device cannot be delivered (no route, discover route = 0), the router sends a Network Status back to the source of the frame, with the frame's destination in the destination address field.

dimm.stock_note: no Network Status to the source of three frames for which the bulb has no route (13 s)

tw.stock_note: no Network Status to the source of three frames for which the bulb has no route (13 s)

tests.ambiguous: 3.6.3.7 leaves to the implementation when a link counts as failed; the test sends five frames, none of which is acknowledged by the next hop, and 3.6.3.3 requires a report for a frame that could not be delivered 'for any reason'
tests.requirement: When the next hop of an established route stops acknowledging, the router reports the failure of a relayed frame to its source with a Network Status naming the frame's destination.
An unknown unicast NWK command addressed to the device is answered with a Network Status with status 0x13 (unknown command), sent to the source of that frame.

dimm.stock_note: no Network Status in answer to NWK command 0x3f (R21 and earlier do not send one)

tw.stock_note: no Network Status in answer to NWK command 0x3f (R21 and earlier do not send one)

tests.requirement: A joined and authenticated device discards a NWK data frame that is not secured.
A secured NWK frame whose frame counter is not above the last one accepted from that sender is rejected.
When no Link Status has been received from a router neighbour for more than nwkRouterAgeLimit (3) periods, its outgoing cost is set to 0 (the entry is stale).

dimm.stock_note: 95 s (more than six periods) after the neighbour's last Link Status the bulb still reports a non-zero outgoing cost for it

tw.stock_note: 95 s (more than six periods) after the neighbour's last Link Status the bulb still reports a non-zero outgoing cost for it

tests.requirement: A router through which a device joins by MAC association sends the Trust Center an Update Device command with the device's addresses and status 0x01 (standard device unsecured join).
On an APS Tunnel command the router sends the embedded command to the named device with NWK security disabled (this is how a joiner gets the network key).

A frame for a child with macRxOnWhenIdle = FALSE is held and handed over after the child's data poll, whose acknowledgement has the frame pending bit set; a poll with nothing waiting is acknowledged with the bit clear.

tests.ambiguous: the unit (superframe period, aBaseSuperframeDuration = 15.36 ms) and the indirect queue itself are defined in IEEE 802.15.4, which is not among the documents the suite reads; the test only requires delivery at 3 s and no delivery at 12 s
tests.requirement: A frame waiting for a sleeping child is kept for nwkTransactionPersistenceTime (0x01f4 superframe periods = 7.68 s) and dropped after that.
A unicast frame from a child for another device is relayed: same NWK source and sequence number, radius decremented, secured again by the relaying router with its own frame counter and address.

A valid End Device Timeout Request from a child is answered with status SUCCESS and a parent information bitmask naming at least one keepalive method; the response has radius 1 and both IEEE addresses in the NWK header.
An End Device Timeout Request with a timeout enumeration outside 0-14 is answered with status INCORRECT_VALUE (0x01).
An End Device Timeout Request with a non-zero End Device Configuration field is answered with status INCORRECT_VALUE (0x01).
A NWK_addr_req for the IEEE address of a router's end device child is answered by the router (also when the request was broadcast to 0xFFFD) with SUCCESS and the child's network address.
An IEEE_addr_req for the network address of a router's end device child is answered by the router with SUCCESS and the child's IEEE address.
A router with a macRxOnWhenIdle = FALSE neighbour passes a broadcast for 0xFFFF on to it as a MAC unicast (indirect transmission allowed); a broadcast for 0xFFFD is not passed to it.

When a router relays a unicast frame of its end device child towards a concentrator (many-to-one route), it first unicasts a Route Record whose NWK source is the child, relay count 1 and relay list holding the router's own address.
A router answers a Route Request for the address of one of its end device children itself, with the child's address as responder address in the Route Reply.
When a child announces that it leaves with Rejoin = 0, its router sends the Trust Center an Update Device command with status 0x02 (device left).
A child's Leave with Rejoin = 1 is not reported to the Trust Center as 'device left': Update Device with status 0x02 is issued only for Rejoin = 0.
A child that negotiated a 10 s timeout and then sends nothing is deleted from the neighbour table when the timeout runs out.
Ageing out a child only deletes the entry; the Trust Center is not told 'device left' (Update Device status 0x02 follows a Leave with Rejoin = 0, nothing else).
A keepalive (MAC data poll, or End Device Timeout Request where only that method is offered) resets the child's timeout counter: a child that keeps sending keepalives is not aged out.

A MAC data poll from a device that is not in the neighbour table makes the router queue a leave message for it: NWK Leave with request = 1, rejoin = 1 and no destination IEEE address, or Mgmt_Leave_req with a null device address and Rejoin = 1.

When a unicast frame whose NWK source is one of the router's end device children arrives from a different MAC source, another router has become the child's parent: the neighbour table entry is deleted.

dimm.stock_note: after two unicast frames of the child arrived through another router the child is still in the neighbour table (End Device Timeout Response SUCCESS)

tw.stock_note: after two unicast frames of the child arrived through another router the child is still in the neighbour table (End Device Timeout Response SUCCESS)

tests.requirement: A broadcast Device_annce for the IEEE address of one of the router's end device children that was relayed by another device (no entry in the broadcast transaction table) deletes the child's neighbour table entry.

A secured Rejoin Request from a known child is answered with a Rejoin Response (status 0, the address already on record, secured like the request, both IEEE addresses) and reported to the Trust Center with Update Device status 0x00 (secured rejoin).

An unsecured Rejoin Request (Trust Center rejoin) in a centralized network is answered with an unsecured Rejoin Response and reported with Update Device status 0x03; the network key then reaches the device through the router.
A Remove Device command from a device other than the Trust Center is ignored; one from the Trust Center naming a child makes the router send that child a NWK Leave with request = 1 and rejoin = 0.

When the device takes a new Trust Center link key it sets the incoming frame counter for that key to 0, so a Trust Center that starts the new key's counter at 0 is accepted: the Confirm Key ends the exchange.

When the Trust Center does not answer the Request Key, the node retries every bdbcTCLinkKeyExchangeTimeout (5 s), up to bdbTCLinkKeyExchangeAttemptsMax attempts (an attribute, default 3), and then leaves the network.

A network key sent by the Trust Center by unicast (under the link key) becomes the alternate key, and the broadcast Switch Key makes it the active key: from then on the device secures its frames with the new key sequence number and never with the old key.
With a new network key all incoming frame counters start at 0 again: a neighbour that restarts its outgoing counter with the new key is accepted after the switch.

tests.ambiguous: 4.4.1.5 says 'shall accept', 4.4.2.3 says the device 'may accept' the same command; R23 allows a policy that refuses it
tests.requirement: A device in the joined and authorized state accepts a network key update that the Trust Center broadcasts with NWK security only (no APS encryption), and switches to it on Switch Key.
A device that holds the new network key as alternate and receives a frame that decrypts under the newer key sequence number switches to that key by itself, without a Switch Key command.

A network key is accepted only from the Trust Center: a unicast Transport Key that is not secured with a link key, sent by another router, is discarded, and a Switch Key from that router does not change the active key.
An APS-secured frame under a unique link key whose frame counter is not above the last one accepted from that device is rejected.
A Remove Device command without APS encryption is dropped; one from the Trust Center, APS-encrypted, naming the router itself makes it leave the network.

tests.requirement: The Identify command sets IdentifyTime to its Identify Time field; a value of 0 stops identifying.
While identifying, the device answers a unicast Identify Query with an Identify Query Response sent to the requester, whose Timeout is the current IdentifyTime.
A device that is not identifying takes no action on an Identify Query: no Identify Query Response is sent.
A finding & binding target answers the initiator's Identify Query, which is broadcast to 0xffff, with a unicast Identify Query Response while it is identifying, and stays silent when it is not.
When IdentifyTime reaches zero the device stops identifying: the attribute stays 0 and Identify Query is no longer answered.
